label: GPT-6.1 Sol
output:
Hi Mikaela, sorry it’s taken me a bit to get back to you. You were such a help when Dave did his shoulder, least I can do is give you the honest version!

We started on 21 September, after mating had started. We’re milking 290, mostly 3-way crossbreds. We skip Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday afternoon milkings, so four once-a-days a week, but mornings are still 5.15 every day. No sleep-ins unfortunately 😂

Production-wise, going off the Fonterra app we’re about 6% down on milksolids for the same weeks last year. Our rep had said to expect 8–10%, so it’s been better than we’d braced ourselves for. That’s only comparing one season with another though, not a proper trial, and I can’t tell you yet what it’ll look like come March. I wouldn’t want you budgeting on our 6% as a guarantee.

The cells did jump. We were around 110,000 and went up to about 180,000 in the first three weeks. Back around 135,000 now, so they’ve settled, but it wasn’t a case of changing the roster and carrying on without watching them.

The worst bit was a heifer with mastitis that went bad on a skipped afternoon. We didn’t pick it up until the next morning and she lost a quarter. That’s the bit I’d really want you to know about before deciding. The afternoon milking might be off, but you still need to be checking cows on those days. You’ve got to be right on your game with that and teat spraying or it bites you. I wouldn’t want to dress that up as all easy.

The cows themselves came round quicker than I expected. About four days of bellowing at the gate and then they were fine with it.

Lameness has been a big plus here. We’ve got four on the lame list now compared with eleven this time last year. Our back paddocks are a 1.8km walk, so cutting out some of those trips is no small thing.

But honestly the biggest difference has been for us and the staff. The first Sunday afternoon we skipped, Dave and I went to Hamilton to see the grandkids. First Sunday afternoon off in spring in twenty-odd years. Felt quite strange heading away!

Kieran, our 2IC, said it’s the first spring he hasn’t wanted to quit by October. That probably tells you more about the hours than I can. With Tom’s knees being bad, I reckon getting those afternoons off would help him more than anything, and I can see why you’re looking at it with your young fella talking about leaving too.

For us, honestly, I wouldn’t go back. The hours alone are worth the 6% to me. But that’s our call for our place, not me saying you should do it. There’s a production cost, the cells need watching and that heifer was a pretty rotten reminder that you can miss something between milkings.

Come and have a look through our shed rosters and numbers with me at the field day on the 19th. Happy to show you the actual figures, bad bits included. Or ring me whenever suits and we can have a proper yarn. Much easier than me trying to type it all with these useless thumbs!
